messages:
marco: Heads up — since last night we started seeing a spike in provisioning failures in eu-west3. Root cause looks like the new wear-balancer daemon kicking background rebalance jobs that overlap with GPU launches. provisioning p95 jumped from ~600ms to >2s. ops-bot posted a scrub backlog alert at 00:12 UTC.

jia: :eyes: can you paste the logs? are these plain evictions or churn from scrub/fstrim?

marco: quick dump from node gnode-eu3-42: ```May 03 00:11:58 gnode kernel: nvme0: async rebalance start (src /dev/nvme1)
May 03 00:12:02 gnode scrubber[2143]: scrub queued: 87 items, rate=120/s
May 03 00:12:05 gnode kubelet[1]: evicting pod redwood-gpu-batch-7 (OOM?)```

sofia: hmm scrub + rebalance + pod evictions = IO saturation window. we've seen similar when cleaner jobs overlap with scaling events. Did we change rebalance schedule?

marco: We flipped the balancer to aggressive mode last week to level wear across hosts faster. That increases concurrent streaming transfers between local NVMe devices. Works fine when cluster is idle but bad during batch job spikes.

nate: Could we make the balancer low-priority i/o or gate it behind provision-rate? e.g. don't run rebalance if ephemeral.provision.rate > 10/min. That would avoid interfering with launches.

sofia: Agreed. Also we should add a short-stall window during autoscaler events: when scaling.up or scaling.down true, pause balancing for 5m.

jia: We should measure impact first. Add metrics: nvme.rebalance.ops, nvme.rebalance.bytes, ephemeral.provision.latency.p95. Then do a 5% host canary with agressive mode to compare.

marco: Proposal: new config flags + rollout plan:
1) feature flag: balancer.mode = {off, conservative, aggressive}
2) dynamic gating: balancer.min_idle_provision_rate = 10/min
3) i/o niceness: balancer.ionice_class = 3 (best-effort)
4) autoscale pause: balancer.pause_on_autoscale = true (window=5m)

Example deploy command: ```redwoodctl infra set-config balancer.mode=conservative balancer.ionice_class=3 --env=eu-west3```

nate: For canary: pick pool eu-west3-a, 5% hosts (tag canary=balancer-v2). Run for 24h, compare ephemeral.provision.latency.p95 and nvme.scrub.backlog. If provisioning latency improves and wear delta acceptable, ramp.

sofia: Also add circuit-breaker: if nvme.err.rate or scrub.backlog exceeds threshold, stop rebalance immediately and annotate nodes with "no-rebalance" so autoscaler isn't penalized.

marco: I'll open a quick PR with the flag defaults and add the metrics. Can we get someone to own the canary monitoring tomorrow morning?

jia: I'll own monitoring for the canary window. I'll hook up alert thresholds: ephemeral.provision.latency.p95 > 1s -> page on-call. nvme.scrub.backlog > 200 -> paging too.

ops-bot: ALERT: scrub-backlog-high on cluster eu-west3 at 00:12:05 UTC (count=87).

deploy-bot: Deploy started: balancer v2 rollout (canary) -> eu-west3-a (5 hosts). ID: dpl-20260503-07

marco: thanks — will post PR link and timeline in this thread. For immediate mitigation I've scaled cleaner concurrency down to 2 on all eu-west3 hosts (quick patch) so we stop thrashing while canary rolls out.

nate: one more ops note: we should consider adding a small local-cache throttle so rebalance transfers yield after X MB in 1s. That would bound short-term IOPS spikes.

sofia: good call. Add it to PR as balancer.max_burst_mb=64.

marco: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/+/2345 — config + metrics + docs. Canaries start in 10m.

jia: monitoring hooks added, will report back with metrics snapshot after 1h. :thumbsup:

marco: closing loop here: if you see provisioning errors in the next hour reply in this thread and I'll revert the canary immediately.
